Before fiscal 2017 the file carries a number for each person and the rows under one number are added together; from fiscal 2017 it carries names, and two rows are added together only when the name is rare enough to follow, the department is the same and the hours fit one person. Otherwise each row counts separately, so two people who share a name are never merged. The middle employee is the middle value of everyone paid anything in the year, part-year and part-time staff included, because hours are on file only from fiscal 2017; the “full year” column is the middle of those with full-time hours. In this file a full-time year is 2,080 paid hours in every fiscal year from 2017 to 2025 and 2,160 in fiscal 2026 (27 fortnights of 80 hours rather than 26), so every yearly amount for fiscal 2026 is about 3.8% larger than a like-for-like year. tables.how: Tax returns covering eleven months or more in which City payments were at least 25% of revenue. Bonuses are from the compensation schedule, from the organization’s own funds, counted where they come to $10,000 or more between all listed people. The top officer is the best-paid current officer whose title says chief executive, executive director or president; a raise compares that person’s total pay (from the organization and related organizations) with the year before, and is tested only where the person was already listed with pay two returns back, so that the earlier figure is a full year. The marks: revenue less expenses below zero by 2% of spending or more; the employee count on the return down by a tenth or more on the previous return (ten or more employees); a federal audit with findings for the year (from the federal audit findings on file); a Public Health or homelessness contract monitor recording a programme below standard or under 80% of contracted objectives for the City fiscal year that the tax year mostly covers (from the City’s contract-monitoring results on file); and, for the 60 organizations paid most, a scorecard verdict of “only its own reports” or “no result on record”, which is not tied to a year. Ranked by the number of year-specific marks, then by the money. Where the organization’s tax number was matched by hand and has not been verified, the last column says so. All 85 rows are listed: 68 with a difficulty measured in the same year and 17 where the only mark is that no result recorded by anyone else was found.
tables.limits: None of these combinations is improper in itself. A deficit can be planned spending of reserves or a grant booked in another year; staff counts fall when a programme ends; an audit finding says a requirement or control was not met, and most are fixed; a monitoring shortfall concerns one programme of many and several fall in pandemic years. A bonus may have been earned the year before or owed under contract, and a raise may follow a promotion or a market review; pay on the return is for the calendar year ending inside the tax year. The monitoring list on disk holds the strongest 60 of 96 provider-years, so some shortfalls are missed. The pattern is a reason to ask what the board tied the payment to, nothing more.

tables.how: The latest return covering eleven months or more for each organization. The top officer is the best-paid current officer whose title says chief executive, executive director or president (failing that, the best-paid current officer); pay is the total on Part VII of the return, from the organization and related organizations. Organizations are grouped by revenue into six bands and each is set against the middle top-officer pay of its band, computed across all City-paid organizations with a return. Listed: those where City payments were at least 25% of revenue, ranked by pay against the band. “Pay to all listed people” adds up everyone on Part VII paid by the organization and divides by total expenses. City money is spread onto the tax year by days of overlap; for the two largest child-care voucher agencies it is taken from the project’s child-care analysis. Where the organization’s tax number was matched by hand and has not been verified, the last column says so. All 186 such organizations are listed, out of 413 whose top officer's pay could be set against size.
tables.limits: Pay is set by each board and no rule caps it; the tax rule is only that it be reasonable for the job. Revenue is a rough measure of the job: an organization that passes most of its money through to others, runs clinics with physicians, or manages buildings is harder or easier to lead than its revenue suggests. A small organization’s chief can be its main programme worker, so a high share of revenue is common there. Pay can include a one-time payout, and a year with two chief executives shows only one.
